title: M-QUEST - Meme Question-Understanding Evaluation on Semantics and Toxicity

bias_targets.methodology: Zero-shot evaluation of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) using multiple-choice question-answering tasks (M-QUEST benchmark) to assess their ability to detect and semantically explain toxic or hateful rhetoric targeting the LGBTQ+ community in multimodal memes.

Assessing VLM performance on multiple-choice reasoning questions to determine if the models can identify and explain implicit religious stereotypes (e.g., Islamophobia) and harmful intent within internet memes using background knowledge and visual-textual mapping.

Evaluating VLMs on a compositional QA benchmark to detect misogynistic content and properly reason about the underlying semantic mechanisms (such as objectification or cyberbullying) in meme contexts.

Testing VLM capabilities to classify and logically explain hate speech and disparagement directed at individuals based on skin color, race, or ethnicity using paired toxicity and semantic reasoning questions.

Using multiple-choice QA pairs to test whether Vision-Language Models can correctly identify and logically reason about age-based discrimination and problematic behaviors (e.g., involving minors) depicted in memes.
